36# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

37# Math helpers 

38# 

39# `_dirichlet_grad` mirrors the reference implementation in 

40# ``ATen/native/Distributions.h`` (``dirichlet_grad_one`` and its private 

41# beta-gradient helpers), which express the reparameterized Dirichlet gradient 

42# as a piecewise function of ``x`` (the sampled value), ``alpha`` (the 

43# concentration) and ``total = sum(alpha)``. Each branch is a careful 

44# asymptotic / rational approximation of ``-(d/dalpha cdf)/pdf`` of the 

45# corresponding Beta distribution. Replicating the exact branching structure 

46# (instead of the naive closed-form ``x * (digamma(total)-digamma(alpha)+log(x))``) 

47# is required to match PyTorch numerically, since the closed form is only 

48# asymptotically correct and diverges from the reference for the moderate 

49# ``alpha`` / near-boundary ``x`` values that occur in practice. 

50# 

51# All work is done in the input dtype (float32/float64) to match the reference 

52# ``accscalar_t``; the result is cast back to the input dtype at the boundary. 

53# 

54# Control-flow structure: the reference is an element-wise ``if -> return`` 

55# cascade, where a hit branch skips all the later ones. Triton's ``tl.where`` 

56# evaluates both sides eagerly, so the previous implementation computed every 

57# branch (small / large / mid / rational) for every element and merged with 

58# ``tl.where`` -- a large amount of dead computation. Instead, the piecewise 

59# math is expressed as *scalar* functions (real ``if`` control flow, lazy 

60# evaluation) and mapped over the tile with ``tl.map_elementwise`` (requires 

61# Triton >= 3.6). Warp-level divergence still exists within a warp, but 

62# non-taken branches are no longer unconditionally evaluated and register 

63# live ranges shrink considerably. 

64# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

151# This kernel carries far more per-element state than a typical pointwise op 

152# (digamma reflection/series state, the Taylor/saddle-point/rational 

153# sub-branches, many coefficient tables), so register pressure grows quickly 

154# with the tile size. On NVIDIA hardware the default 512-wide tile measures 

155# measurably slower than a 128-wide 1-D tile (fp32 [64,1024,16]: ~0.22 ms vs 

156# ~0.13 ms; fp64 is compute-bound and roughly flat), so use a dedicated 

157# config for NVIDIA and keep the vendor default elsewhere. 

158_DIRICHLET_GRAD_CONFIG = ( 

159 CodeGenConfig( 

160 128, 

161 (65536, 65536, 65536), 

162 32, 

163 True, 

164 prefer_1d_tile=True, 

165 ) 

166 if device.vendor == vendors.NVIDIA 

167 else None

171@triton.jit 

172def _div_rn(a, b): 

173 # IEEE round-to-nearest division. ``tl.div_rn`` is only available for 

174 # float32 (it maps to a fast correctly-rounded intrinsic); for float64 the 

175 # plain ``/`` operator is already correctly rounded, so fall back to it. 

176 # ``b.dtype`` is a compile-time attribute, so this ``if`` is specialized 

177 # away and the fp32-only intrinsic is never instantiated for fp64 inputs. 

178 # ``b`` (the denominator) is always a tensor in the call sites below, which 

179 # makes the dtype check reliable even when ``a`` is a python scalar. 

180 if b.dtype == tl.float32: 

181 return tl.div_rn(a, b) 

182 else: 

183 return a / b

186@triton.jit 

187def _digamma_one(x): 

188 # Cephes-style digamma. Ported from ATen::native::digamma_one so that the 

189 # result is bit-for-bit close to the reference implementation used inside 

190 # ``dirichlet_grad_one``. This is a *scalar* function (evaluated per 

191 # element via ``tl.map_elementwise``), so the branches below are real 

192 # control flow: expensive math on a non-taken branch is not evaluated. 

193 PI: tl.constexpr = 3.1415926535897932384626433832795028841971 

194 PSI_10: tl.constexpr = 2.25175258906672110764 

195 

196 # x == 0 or a negative integer maps to +inf, matching the reference. 

197 if x <= 0.0: 

198 if x == tl_extra_shim.floor(x): 

199 return tl.zeros_like(x) + float("inf") 

200 

201 additional_summand = tl.zeros_like(x) 

202 y = x 

203 

204 # For x < 0 the reflection x -> 1 - x is applied; ``-pi / tan(pi * x)`` 

205 # uses a correctly-rounded division so the accumulation matches the 

206 # reference ``digamma_one`` rounding. 

207 if x < 0.0: 

208 additional_summand = _div_rn(-PI, tl_extra_shim.tan(PI * x)) 

209 y = 1.0 - x 

210 

211 # Push y to be >= 10 (matches the C++ ``while (y < 10)``). After the 

212 # reflection y is strictly positive, so at most 10 unit increments are 

213 # ever needed -- the previous fixed 80-iteration loop evaluated the 

214 # division unconditionally on every iteration. 

215 result = tl.zeros_like(x) 

216 for _ in range(10): 

217 if y < 10.0: 

218 # ``tl.div_rn`` (IEEE round-to-nearest) is used for the harmonic 

219 # sum; Triton's tensor ``/`` is an approximate 1-ULP division 

220 # whose error would be amplified by ``1/alpha`` inside the small 

221 # branch of ``dirichlet_grad_one``. 

222 result = result - _div_rn(1.0, y) 

223 y = y + 1.0 

224 

225 # Exact value at the loop boundary. 

226 if y == 10.0: 

227 return result + PSI_10 + additional_summand 

228 

229 # Asymptotic digamma for y > 10. 

230 a0 = 8.33333333333333333333e-2 

231 a1 = -2.10927960927960927961e-2 

232 a2 = 7.57575757575757575758e-3 

233 a3 = -4.16666666666666666667e-3 

234 a4 = 3.96825396825396825397e-3 

235 a5 = -8.33333333333333333333e-3 

236 a6 = 8.33333333333333333333e-2 

237 series = tl.zeros_like(x) 

238 if y < 1.0e17: 

239 z = _div_rn(1.0, y * y) 

240 # Horner evaluation of the asymptotic polynomial A[0..6] (Cephes 

241 # ``polevl`` with degree 6); ``series = z * poly`` reproduces 

242 # ``y = z * polevl(z, A, 6)``. 

243 poly = (((((a6 * z + a5) * z + a4) * z + a3) * z + a2) * z + a1) * z + a0 

244 series = z * poly 

245 

246 return result + tl_extra_shim.log(y) - _div_rn(0.5, y) - series + additional_summand

249@triton.jit 

250def _beta_grad_alpha_small(x, alpha, beta): 

251 # Taylor expansion of the reparameterized Beta(alpha,beta) gradient around x=0. 

252 factor = _digamma_one(alpha) - _digamma_one(alpha + beta) - tl_extra_shim.log(x) 

253 numer = tl.zeros_like(x) + 1.0 

254 # The series is dominated by ``factor / alpha``; for tiny ``alpha`` any 

255 # rounding in ``1 / alpha`` is amplified, so use correctly-rounded division. 

256 inv_alpha = _div_rn(1.0, alpha) 

257 series = _div_rn(numer, alpha) * (factor + inv_alpha) 

258 for i in range(1, 11): 

259 casted_i = i 

260 numer = numer * (casted_i - beta) * x / casted_i 

261 denom = alpha + casted_i 

262 inv_denom = _div_rn(1.0, denom) 

263 series = series + _div_rn(numer, denom) * (factor + inv_denom) 

264 result = x * tl_extra_shim.pow(1.0 - x, -beta) * series 

265 if result != result: 

266 return tl.zeros_like(result) 

267 return result

270@triton.jit 

271def _beta_grad_beta_small(x, alpha, beta): 

272 # Taylor expansion of the reparameterized Beta(alpha,beta) gradient around x=1. 

273 factor = _digamma_one(alpha + beta) - _digamma_one(beta) 

274 numer = tl.zeros_like(x) + 1.0 

275 betas = tl.zeros_like(x) + 1.0 

276 dbetas = tl.zeros_like(x) 

277 series = _div_rn(factor, alpha) 

278 for i in range(1, 9): 

279 casted_i = i 

280 numer = numer * (-x / casted_i) 

281 dbetas = dbetas * (beta - casted_i) + betas 

282 betas = betas * (beta - casted_i) 

283 series = series + _div_rn(numer, alpha + casted_i) * (dbetas + factor * betas) 

284 result = -tl_extra_shim.pow(1.0 - x, 1.0 - beta) * series 

285 if result != result: 

286 return tl.zeros_like(result) 

287 return result

290@triton.jit 

291def _beta_grad_alpha_mid(x, alpha, beta): 

292 # Rice saddle-point expansion for alpha, beta both large. 

293 total = alpha + beta 

294 mean = alpha / total 

295 std = tl_extra_shim.sqrt(alpha * beta / (total + 1.0)) / total 

296 near_mean = (mean - 0.1 * std <= x) & (x <= mean + 0.1 * std) 

297 

298 # Real branch: previously both the polynomial form and the (much more 

299 # expensive) saddle-point form were computed and selected afterwards with 

300 # ``tl.where``. 

301 if near_mean: 

302 # Polynomial form valid close to the mode. ``b2..b4`` are powers of 

303 # beta; the Cephes polynomial is, in alpha, degree 4 with descending 

304 # powers of beta: beta^4, beta^3, beta^2, beta^1, beta^0 (inside the 

305 # last factor). 

306 b2 = beta * beta 

307 b3 = b2 * beta 

308 b4 = b2 * b2 

309 poly = 47.0 * x * b4 + alpha * ( 

310 (43.0 + 20.0 * (16.0 + 27.0 * beta) * x) * b3 

311 + alpha 

312 * ( 

313 3.0 * (59.0 + 180.0 * beta - 90.0 * x) * b2 

314 + alpha 

315 * ( 

316 (453.0 + 1620.0 * beta * (1.0 - x) - 455.0 * x) * beta 

317 + alpha * (8.0 * (1.0 - x) * (135.0 * beta - 11.0)) 

318 ) 

319 ) 

320 ) 

321 prefactor_num = _div_rn( 

322 (1.0 + 12.0 * alpha) * (1.0 + 12.0 * beta), total * total 

323 ) 

324 prefactor_den = ( 

325 12960.0 * alpha * alpha * alpha * beta * beta * (1.0 + 12.0 * total) 

326 ) 

327 return _div_rn(prefactor_num, (1.0 - x)) * _div_rn(poly, prefactor_den) 

328 

329 prefactor = _div_rn(-x, tl_extra_shim.sqrt(2.0 * alpha * beta / total)) 

330 stirling = ( 

331 (1.0 + 1.0 / (12.0 * alpha) + 1.0 / (288.0 * alpha * alpha)) 

332 * (1.0 + 1.0 / (12.0 * beta) + 1.0 / (288.0 * beta * beta)) 

333 / (1.0 + 1.0 / (12.0 * total) + 1.0 / (288.0 * total * total)) 

334 ) 

335 term1_num = ( 

336 2.0 * alpha * alpha * (x - 1.0) + alpha * beta * (x - 1.0) - x * (beta * beta) 

337 ) 

338 # ``axbx`` is exactly the previous ``term3_den`` expression, computed once. 

339 axbx = alpha * (x - 1.0) + beta * x 

340 term1_den = ( 

341 tl_extra_shim.sqrt(2.0 * alpha / beta) 

342 * (total * tl_extra_shim.sqrt(total)) 

343 * axbx 

344 * axbx 

345 ) 

346 term1 = _div_rn(term1_num, term1_den) 

347 # ``log(alpha / (total * x))`` is shared by ``term2`` and ``term4_base``. 

348 log_a_over_total_x = tl_extra_shim.log(_div_rn(alpha, total * x)) 

349 term2 = 0.5 * log_a_over_total_x 

350 term3_num = tl_extra_shim.sqrt(8.0 * alpha * beta / total) 

351 term3 = _div_rn(term3_num, axbx) 

352 # ``term4_base`` is a difference of two large log-terms and is numerically 

353 # delicate near the mode (it can approach zero, and ``pow(base, -1.5)`` 

354 # amplifies any rounding). The reference evaluates the quotients in 

355 # ``accscalar_t`` with IEEE round-to-nearest division; Triton's plain 

356 # ``/`` on tensors is an approximate (1-ULP) division, so we use 

357 # ``tl.div_rn`` (correctly rounded) here to reproduce the reference's 

358 # rounding and keep the saddle-point regime within tolerance. 

359 log_b_over_total_1mx = tl_extra_shim.log(_div_rn(beta, total * (1.0 - x))) 

360 term4_base = beta * log_b_over_total_1mx + alpha * log_a_over_total_x 

361 # ``pow(base, -1.5)`` expressed as ``1 / (base * sqrt(base))`` so that the 

362 # exponent stays in the base's dtype (``tl_extra_shim.pow`` with a python 

363 # scalar exponent mismatches dtypes for float64). 

364 term4 = _div_rn(1.0, term4_base * tl_extra_shim.sqrt(term4_base)) 

365 if x < mean: 

366 term1234 = term1 + term2 * (term3 + term4) 

367 else: 

368 term1234 = term1 + term2 * (term3 - term4) 

369 return stirling * prefactor * term1234

458 ua = pow_u0 * pow_a2 

459 p = p + ua * (C0_020 + b * (C0_021 + b * (C0_022 + b * C0_023))) 

460 q = q + ua * (C1_020 + b * (C1_021 + b * (C1_022 + b * C1_023))) 

461 

462 ua = pow_u1 * pow_a0 

463 p = p + ua * (C0_100 + b * (C0_101 + b * (C0_102 + b * C0_103))) 

464 q = q + ua * (C1_100 + b * (C1_101 + b * (C1_102 + b * C1_103))) 

465 

466 ua = pow_u1 * pow_a1 

467 p = p + ua * (C0_110 + b * (C0_111 + b * (C0_112 + b * C0_113))) 

468 q = q + ua * (C1_110 + b * (C1_111 + b * (C1_112 + b * C1_113))) 

469 

470 ua = pow_u1 * pow_a2 

471 p = p + ua * (C0_120 + b * (C0_121 + b * (C0_122 + b * C0_123))) 

472 q = q + ua * (C1_120 + b * (C1_121 + b * (C1_122 + b * C1_123))) 

473 

474 ua = pow_u2 * pow_a0 

475 p = p + ua * (C0_200 + b * (C0_201 + b * (C0_202 + b * C0_203))) 

476 q = q + ua * (C1_200 + b * (C1_201 + b * (C1_202 + b * C1_203))) 

477 

478 ua = pow_u2 * pow_a1 

479 p = p + ua * (C0_210 + b * (C0_211 + b * (C0_212 + b * C0_213))) 

480 q = q + ua * (C1_210 + b * (C1_211 + b * (C1_212 + b * C1_213))) 

481 

482 ua = pow_u2 * pow_a2 

483 p = p + ua * (C0_220 + b * (C0_221 + b * (C0_222 + b * C0_223))) 

484 q = q + ua * (C1_220 + b * (C1_221 + b * (C1_222 + b * C1_223))) 

485 

486 approx = _div_rn(x * (_digamma_one(total) - _digamma_one(alpha)), beta) 

487 return _div_rn(p, q) * approx

490if _HAS_MAP_ELEMENTWISE: 

491 

492 @pointwise_dynamic( 

493 is_tensor=[True, True, True], 

494 promotion_methods=[(0, 1, 2, "DEFAULT")], 

495 config=_DIRICHLET_GRAD_CONFIG, 

496 ) 

497 @triton.jit 

498 def _dirichlet_grad_func(x, alpha, total): 

499 # ``pointwise_dynamic`` provides the tensor tile (load / store / mask); 

500 # the piecewise implementation runs element by element inside 

501 # ``tl.map_elementwise`` so the scalar ``if`` cascade is lazy, matching 

502 # ATen's ``gpu_kernel(... dirichlet_grad_one(...))`` structure. The 

503 # reference ``dirichlet_grad_one`` accumulates in ``accscalar_t`` which 

504 # equals the input dtype (float for float, double for double); the inputs 

505 # are already promoted to that dtype by ``pointwise_dynamic``. 

506 return tl.map_elementwise(_dirichlet_grad_one, x, alpha, total).to(x.dtype) 

507 

508 

509def _dirichlet_grad(x, alpha, total): 

510 logger.debug("GEMS DIRICHLET_GRAD") 

511 if not _HAS_MAP_ELEMENTWISE: 

512 raise NotImplementedError( 

513 "_dirichlet_grad requires tl.map_elementwise (Triton >= 3.6); " 

514 "not available on this backend." 

515 ) 

516 # The ATen reference only implements the AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES path 

517 # (float32 / float64); reject other dtypes explicitly to match the CUDA 

518 # dispatcher behaviour. 

519 assert x.dtype in ( 

520 torch.float32, 

521 torch.float64, 

522 ), f"_dirichlet_grad only supports float32/float64, got {x.dtype}" 

523 return _dirichlet_grad_func(x, alpha, total) 

524

529 raise NotImplementedError( 

530 "_dirichlet_grad requires tl.map_elementwise (Triton >= 3.6); " 

531 "not available on this backend." 

532 ) 

533 assert x.dtype in ( 

534 torch.float32, 

535 torch.float64, 

536 ), f"_dirichlet_grad only supports float32/float64, got {x.dtype}" 

537 _dirichlet_grad_func(x, alpha, total, out0=out) 

538 return out
